articles.title: Music Industry Moves: Jesse Jo Stark Signs With WME, Rebecca Allen Steps Down at Universal Music U.K.
articles.summary: Singer-songwriter-actress and Chrome Hearts co-creative director Jesse Jo Stark has signed with WME for worldwide representation in all areas. Stark’s new album “Muse” is out Nov.
body: Following the merger of EMI and Island in July 2024, Allen was appointed as president of the new Audience & Media division, and subsequently promoted to the newly-formed, “first-of-its-kind” leadership role of chief artist and strategy officer in December 2025. Previously, she was president and later co-president of the relaunched EMI (alongside Jo Charrington), following her role as president of Decca from 2017 to 2020 – becoming the first female president at a Universal Music U.K. label.

“I leave enormously proud of what we’ve created together, grateful for the friendships, the adventures, the lessons and the laughter, and for 27 years that have shaped me in more ways than I probably even realise yet,” Allen wrote in a farewell letter to staff, per MW. “It’s been quite a ride. I can’t thank you all enough for being on this journey with me. Love to you all.”

articles.title: ‘A tipping point of ickiness’: Welsh star Tom Rhys Harries on playing eyelid-snipping DC supervillain Clayface
articles.summary: He cut his teeth playing rock stars and pretty posh boys. Speaking from his LA home, the actor talks about landing his first blockbuster lead in the grisly DC horror. Will it be too shocking for comic book fans?
body: Exactly 13 years ago this month, Tom Rhys Harries was hanging by his ankles from a meat hook every night. Playing a teenage rock’n’roll idol abducted by gangsters in a revival of Jez Butterworth’s Mojo, Harries was fresh out of drama school and the only unknown in a cast led by Ben Whishaw and Rupert Grint. The Guardian’s Michael Billington likened him to “an embryonic Elvis”.

Now the 36-year-old Cardiff-born actor has the title role in Clayface, a violent DC Comics supervillain blockbuster set in Batman’s stomping ground, Gotham City. This puts him in the company of fellow Brits in the comic-book universe, such as Tom Holland (Spider-Man), Robert Pattinson (Batman) and David Jonsson, recently announced as the new Black Panther. “I felt ready to do this,” says Harries. “Had I been younger, I’d have been suffocated by the insecurity of wanting to do a good job but not having that quiet trust in getting there.”

Harries has earned the right to relax. He spent three months auditioning to play the severely mutilated protagonist of Clayface for producers James Gunn (Guardians of the Galaxy) and Matt Reeves (The Batman). How did he stay sane all that time? “I didn’t.”

articles.title: Battle of the Booths: Paramount Brings its Iconic Arch to Cannes as Eye-Catching Mipcom Stands Reflect Market Realities
articles.summary: Step outside Le Palais des Festivals in Cannes this week, where Mipcom is in full swing, and you might do a double take. Because nestled between the conference center and the French Riviera is an exact (well, 90% scale) replica of Paramount Studios’ iconic Bronson Gate.
body: “We wanted to do something different,” Lasarenko says of the project, which took design agency Glow Studios around three weeks to build and ship over from the U.K. Glow founder James Schnauer even flew out to L.A. to photograph the arch so he could “reverse engineer the detail” and make a 3D-printed model. (The finished result is so detailed it includes the intricate filigrees found on the original.) “It feels like you’re having an experience and bring our clients something that they can’t get anywhere else,” says Lasarenko.

Paramount’s is not the only stand-out booth at this year’s confab, which is organized by RX France. The newly-expanded Banijay Entertainment, who occupy a prime position directly in front of the Palais on the Croisette, have returned with the same two-storey, wooden stand they first debuted in 2022, in keeping with its environmental mission.

The season’s second episode, airing a week later on Oct. 27 in tandem with the kickoff of the NBA season, brings together Shaquille O’Neal and Kevin Durant to tackle another perennial debate: the greatest starting five in NBA history. Following the first two episodes, Rushmore will move to a bi-weekly release cadence.
Later this season, Larry David and Jerry Seinfeld will join Emanuel and Persky for a special episode about comedy GOATs taped during the Netflix Is a Joke festival in May 2026.

articles.title: Ex-gang boss sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
articles.summary: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.
body: Former gang boss Duane "Keffe D" Davis has been sentenced to at least 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur.

A jury found Davis, 63, guilty in September of one count of murder with a deadly weapon for the rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on 7 September 1996. He has said he will appeal the verdict.

Prosecutors argued that although Davis did not fire the gun himself, he was the ringleader of the group that committed the murder. He admitted in his memoir that he had provided the gun used in the crime.
Davis' conviction was the first in a cold case that has intrigued hip-hop fans for nearly 30 years.
points: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.

articles.title: Forever Is Now review – political study of former Irish Green leader is like The Thick of It but with morals
articles.summary: Eamon Ryan is shown to be principled, likable and hard working in a glowing portrait, filmed while serving in the country’s coalition government. This fly-on-the-wall documentary about the former Irish Green party leader and cabinet minister Eamon Ryan reminded me of the political satire The Thick…
body: The title is something that Ryan’s 25-year-old son Tommy repeats over and over. “Forever … forever … forever.” Tommy is autistic and requires full-time care. When Ryan resigns from government, one of his reasons is to spend more time with Tommy. We see the pair of them at the allotment picking raspberries and walking the dog. But other than a quick glimpse of his wife, Victoria, the rest of Ryan’s family life is kept firmly behind closed doors.

Instead, the cameras trail him on the road, talking to angry residents of an Irish town submerged by flood waters (again), and hustling at the UN general assembly in New York and two Cop conferences. At his side is formidable media adviser Edel Hackett (Malcolm Tucker with morals), who sifts through the daily torrent of online abuse, harassment and intimidation slung Ryan’s way.
points: Eamon Ryan is shown to be principled, likable and hard working in a glowing portrait, filmed while serving in the country’s coalition government.

articles.title: Katie Price denies 'any venom' against ex at his rape trial
articles.summary: Kieran Hayler, who denies offences against a girl when she was 13, was married to Price at the time.
body: Katie Price has denied having "any venom" against her ex-husband at his rape trial.
Kieran Hayler is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one of sexual assault against a then-13-year-old girl in West Sussex in 2016, all of which he denies.
When challenged by defence lawyer Arlette Piercy on her view of her ex-husband, Price said: "I don't have any venom against Kieran, it was amicable when we split."
During her evidence to Lewes Crown Court, Price was asked by Piercy if she "loved revenge or is it just TV?".

articles.title: BBC shelves plans for new Archers studio as part of cost-cutting
articles.summary: Cast members on the long-running radio soap are said to be "angry" at plans to move from Birmingham.
body: The BBC has shelved plans to build a new bespoke studio for The Archers in Birmingham as part of its wider drive to cut costs, opening up the possibility that the Radio 4's series could be recorded outside the city for the first time.
The world's longest-running soap opera, The Archers has been recording in the West Midlands city for 75 years.
The BBC had initially pledged to build the show a new studio in the Tea Factory, the corporation's new hub in Digbeth, central Birmingham.
But the broadcaster said it was "currently assessing the BBC's existing studio facilities around the UK as well as other external studio options in the West Midlands".

articles.title: Mag Mag review – giant female ghost loves people to death in Japanese comedy-horror
articles.summary: Sara Minami gives a wonderfully crazed performance in a twisted, fresh take on the genre as Yuriyan Retriever’s debut feature examines infatuation, bullying and beauty norms.
body: Back in the 90s and 00s, Japanese horror (or “J-horror” if you want to save on syllables) was much admired, reasonably widely distributed and sometimes remade in other languages. They never actually stopped making them in Japan, but the results don’t seem to get as much crossover exposure as they used to. That may be because we have quite enough horror getting made closer to home, especially since it’s so remunerative at the box office.

Nevertheless, it’s good to see evidence that the genre keeps evolving in Japan just as it does everywhere else, and there is something tangibly fresh and kicky about this low-budget horror-comedy amalgam. Made by comedian Yuriyan Retriever, an irrepressible character whose dadaist shtick got her on America’s Got Talent twice, makes her directorial debut with this satirical ghost story which sends up male misogyny and women’s obsession with romance alike.
